transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-11-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Amir Khan (ZenHealth CISO), Sara Lopez (Head of Eng), Dr. Emily Chen (Compliance), Raj Patel (DevOps)

Summary: quick call to go through security controls and privacy commitments; customer is healthcare so PHI questions are a priority.

00:00 - Lena: ok everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call
00:12 - Amir: hey thanks, Amir here, CISO at ZenHealth
00:18 - Sara: Sara, eng
00:22 - Dr. Chen: Emily, compliance
00:25 - Raj: Raj, infra
00:30 - Lena: great, i'll hand off to Marco to run through our controls and then we can go deeper on PHI and retention
00:38 - Marco: yep thanks Lena. So high level Redwood has SOC 2 type two, we also have an ISO 27001 program, we can share the report under NDA, it's typically a SOC2+ISO package. our hosted API stores request logs and prompts by default for 30 days for debugging, that can be disabled per account or you can use a dedicated/private deployment where logs don't leave your VPC.
01:05 - Amir: can you confirm that Redwood does not use customer prompts or content to train models? this is critical for us
01:12 - Marco: yes, to be clear — we do not use customer data to train our models. we have a firm policy: customer content is not part of the training corpus. exceptions are only with explicit opt-in, which you would never see for a standard enterprise contract.
01:33 - Dr. Chen: and that includes embeddings and logs, right? not used for continuous improvement
01:38 - Marco: correct, embeddings, prompts, responses are not used for training. we can provide contractual language for DPA/BAA to that effect.
01:48 - Sara: good. about retention, you said 30 days default, can that be shortened or turned off? we have to avoid retaining PHI in hosted env
01:56 - Marco: yes. default store is 30 days for telemetry/debugging, but we offer options: short retention windows, zero retention (no logging) in dedicated or private deployments, and an on-prem agent. for hosted we can turn off persistence at account level and redact PII before it's persisted.
02:20 - Raj: is that per-route or global?
02:23 - Marco: per-config, you can set retention per route or per model. also our routing policies can send PHI traffic to dedicated capacity or private deployment automatically.
02:34 - Amir: encryption — at rest and in transit, what keys do you manage? can we bring our own key (BYOK) to KMS or HSM?
02:42 - Lena: we support customer-managed keys, AWS KMS and HSM integrations, and there is an option for on-prem HSM for private deployments. we also encrypt in transit with TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS for private peering.
02:58 - Raj: if we bring our keys, do logs still contain any plaintext data?
03:03 - Marco: where keys are customer-managed we encrypt artifacts at rest with your keys; logs will be access-controlled and can be redacted. for extra assurance, in dedicated/private we can avoid storing request bodies entirely.
03:15 - Sara: about RBAC and SSO, we use Okta. can we map groups to roles and have audit trails
03:22 - Priya: yes Okta SAML SSO is supported, SSO provisioning via SCIM, and RBAC roles are configurable; admin, developer, viewer, etc. audit logs capture changes and auth events.
03:34 - Amir: how long do audit logs retain? we need 1 year for our internal compliance
03:40 - Marco: default audit log retention is 90 days for hosted, but enterprise add-on supports extended retention to 1+ years. logs can be streamed to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
03:58 - Dr. Chen: for PHI we need a BAA — do you sign BAAs, and are there additional safeguards?
04:05 - Lena: yes we sign BAAs for customers handling PHI. we also recommend dedicated or private deployment for PHI workloads. our DPA and BAA will include data handling commitments and subprocessor lists.
04:20 - Amir: data residency — we need EU-only processing for some workloads
04:24 - Marco: we have regions, processing can be pinned to EU regions; for stronger guarantees we recommend private deployment in your VPC inside the EU region.
04:36 - Sara: what's the difference between Dedicated and Private again? i thought dedicated was reserved machines but still managed by redwood
04:43 - Marco: correct — Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity managed by us in a cloud region; Private gives you a control plane that can be customer-hosted or VPC-connected with customer-managed networking. private is the strongest isolation.
04:56 - Raj: any hardware attestations? like intel SGX or AMD SEV? we use confidential computing for some data flows
05:02 - Marco: we currently don't offer SGX attestation by default; we do support pinned hardware and we can discuss options for on-prem or partner HW with confidential compute — it's an advanced design.
05:20 - Sara: auditability: can we get full request/response logs for incidents? but redacted otherwise
05:26 - Marco: yes you can enable full logging to your S3 destination; then it's under your control. Redwood can store minimal logs or none in private mode.
05:36 - Dr. Chen: about the 'no training' statement — we need contractual language. where would that sit
05:41 - Lena: that will be in the DPA and the main contract; we can include a clause that asserts no retention or training on customer data and no uses for model improvement.
05:51 - Amir: OK. on the technical side, how do you handle PII/PHI detection and redaction? is there auto-redaction?
05:58 - Marco: we have an optional pre-processor pipeline for PII detection, regex and ML-based detectors; can redact or tokenize fields. we also support custom redaction rules provided by the customer.
06:10 - Sara: will that affect latency a lot?
06:13 - Marco: small overhead for pre-processing, typically tens of ms per request depending on rules and throughput.
06:20 - Raj: if we want to do a POC, can we run a small dedicated cluster in our EU region with BYOK and no persistence
06:27 - Priya: yes that's a common pattern; we usually set up a short-term dedicated footprint or private trial and run perf and compliance checks
06:35 - Amir: legal asked whether we can get certs and third-party attestation — you mentioned SOC2; is that SOC2 type two latest report
06:43 - Marco: yes, SOC2 Type II for the last 12 months. we'll provide the latest report under NDA. also ISO 27001 summary and our penetration test attestation.
06:54 - Dr. Chen: do you have a list of subprocessors and data processors
06:58 - Marco: yes, we have a subprocessor list; we'll include that with the SOC2 package. most are cloud infra providers and monitoring
07:08 - Sara: question about model variants and fallback — if we route to a non-hosted model for PHI, is there a possibility of sending data to third-party services
07:18 - Marco: by default all models in our catalog are hosted in our infra; we do not call out to third-party models unless configured, and you can restrict allowed model catalogs at the account level.
07:30 - Lena: quick note — sometimes the transcript generator messes up names, so apologies if you see typos in the notes
07:36 - Amir: haha noted
07:38 - Raj: small question — KV cache, does that persist sensitive context between requests?
07:42 - Marco: KV cache is in-memory for inference and not persisted to disk in private mode; in hosted mode some caches may persist for short windows but can be disabled.
07:55 - Sara: ok we'll need a short doc that summarises all controls and our obligations for the security review board
08:01 - Lena: yes Marco will put together a one-pager and attach the SOC2/ISO and network diagram
08:06 - Marco: action items captured, i'll share docs. also we'll include redwood's BAA sample
08:12 - Dr. Chen: and pricing for dedicated/private? because we will need to budget
08:16 - Lena: we'll share indicative pricing; final pricing depends on committed capacity and whether you need on-prem or private.
08:25 - Amir: anything else? i want to confirm again that nothing is shared to train models
08:30 - Marco: confirmed — no customer content used for training without explicit opt-in; documentation and contract will reflect that
08:36 - Lena: ok recap: Marco to send SOC2/ISO, subprocessor list, network diagram, BAA sample; Priya to schedule tech deep dive; ZenHealth to confirm PII fields and POC scope.
08:50 - Sara: thanks everyone, that was helpful
08:53 - Amir: thanks, expect an email with the compliance questionnaire
08:57 - Lena: thanks, we'll follow up with the docs by monday

End of meeting
